title: Conformalized Physics-Informed Weak Regression for Parameter Estimation in Epidemic Models
Conformalized Physics-Informed Weak Regression for Parameter Estimation in Epidemic Models
summary: Compartment epidemic models are often linear in coefficients that are physical parameters or products of parameters, so parameter estimation can be reduced to closed-form least squares. The paper introduces physics-informed weak regression (PIWR), which integrates the model in time with cubic-spline quadrature, avoids differentiating noisy data, estimates the initial state jointly, and is wrapped with split conformal prediction using simulated epidemics as the calibration population, plus a residual-adaptive factor (PIWR-RACC). Across eleven DINN benchmarks, PIWR or PIR-FD6 is reported to improve on DINN errors by one to four orders of magnitude where sampling resolves the dynamics, each fit takes about a millisecond, and the 90% simultaneous intervals achieve 87–92% empirical coverage in all 88 tested settings.

target.est_compute: CPU, <1 s including data simulation; single PIWR fit is about 0.2 ms
target.quote: With 1 % noise the error of PIR-FD2 grows to 1.2–1.5 %, while PIR-FD6 and PIWR reach 0.12–0.49 %.

requirements.stmt: Formulate the epidemic model in parameter-linear form ẋ = f0(x,t) + A(x,t)θ, with the library A containing no unknown parameters and a map h recovering physical parameters from θ.
requirements.quote: the library A(x, t) ∈Rn×p contains no unknowns

requirements.stmt: For PIWR, use the integrated weak relation x(tj)=x0+Jjθ, with Jj the time integral of the library, instead of differentiating the data.
requirements.quote: The relation is still linear in θ, but it contains the data themselves instead of their derivatives.

requirements.stmt: Evaluate each library entry by a cubic spline with not-a-knot end conditions on the sample grid and integrate the spline exactly to obtain quadrature weights.
requirements.quote: interpolated over t0, . . . , tm−1 by a cubic spline (not-a-knot end conditions), and the spline is integrated exactly from t0 to tj.

requirements.stmt: Estimate the initial state x0 jointly with θ using the augmented system with identity blocks for x0.
requirements.quote: The initial state x0 is treated as n additional unknowns, so that the noise of the first sample is not propagated into every equation.

requirements.stmt: Solve the PIWR least-squares problem by a numerically stable orthogonal factorization or SVD-based least squares, not by explicitly forming the normal equations.
requirements.quote: In implementation, we do not form the normal equations (16), whose condition number is the square of that of MD.

requirements.stmt: Column-scale the regression matrix to unit column norm before the solve; scaling is a change of variables and leaves the minimizer unchanged.
requirements.cite: Sections 3.1 and 3.2, equations (11) and implementation after (18)
requirements.quote: the columns are scaled to unit norm before the solve

requirements.stmt: For the synthetic benchmarks, add compartment-wise noise with standard deviation ε times the maximum absolute true compartment value over the time grid.
requirements.quote: add noise per compartment c as  ̃xc(ti) = xc(ti)+ε maxt|xc(t)| ξi, ξi ∼N(0, 1)

requirements.stmt: For conformal calibration, draw calibration parameters from a prior box of ±50 % around literature values, capped at 1 for probabilities and [0,c] for parameters whose literature value is zero.
requirements.quote: The prior box is ±50 % around the literature values (capped at 1 for probabilities, and [0, c] for the three parameters whose literature value is zero)

requirements.stmt: Use the maximum normalized error over all parameters as the split-conformal nonconformity score, then form simultaneous intervals with the corresponding quantile.
requirements.quote: To obtain intervals that hold for all k parameters at once, we use the maximum normalized error as the nonconformity score

requirements.stmt: For PIWR-RACC, compute the residual-adaptive factor h = 1 + R/Rbar, with Rbar the median residual on 200 tuning draws, and apply h to scores and intervals.
requirements.quote: with  ̄R the median residual on 200 tuning draws, and use it in the score (20) and the intervals (21).

requirements.stmt: Use 999 calibration problems and α=0.1 for the 90 % simultaneous intervals, with tuning done on separate draws.
requirements.quote: The calibration uses n = 999 problems and α = 0.1.

requirements.stmt: Recover physical parameters through ω=h(θ) and, when uncertainty in ω is reported, propagate the coefficient covariance by the delta method.
requirements.quote: The physical parameters are ˆω = h(ˆθ). Their uncertainty follows from the delta method

requirements.stmt: For the COVID-19 SIDR benchmark, use N=59·10^6, initial state S0=N−1 and I0=1, parameters α=0.191, β=0.05, γ=0.0294, and 100 equally spaced samples on [0,500] days.
requirements.cite: Section 2 worked example and Appendix A.1
requirements.quote: 100 equally spaced samples on [0, 500] days (∆t = 5.05 days) of the solution with (α, β, γ) = (0.191, 0.05, 0.0294)

requirements.stmt: Report errors as percent of the actual parameter value, using the median over estimated parameters of a model when summarizing a model.
requirements.quote: Errors are reported in percent of the actual value, as the median over the estimated parameters of a model.

requirements.stmt: Generate synthetic benchmark trajectories with LSODA at relative and absolute tolerances of 10^-10.
requirements.quote: integrated with LSODA (Petzold, 1983) at relative and absolute tolerances of 10−10.

assumptions.gap: The paper does not give the random seed or specify whether the Table 2 PIWR value 0.124 % is from one noise realization, a median over realizations, or a repeated-fit median.
assumptions.chosen: Use a single fixed-seed realization for the point estimate, then check stability over 1,000 realizations at the literature values.
assumptions.quote: for ε = 1 %, on 1,000 noise realizations at the literature values.

assumptions.gap: The paper says row scaling is selected per model on tuning draws but does not state whether the SIDR PIWR run uses Dn=In or compartment-max scaling.
assumptions.chosen: Use Dn=In for SIDR unless a separate tuning run on 100 draws says otherwise.
assumptions.quote: whether to use it (Dn = In otherwise) is decided per model and estimator on a tuning set (section 5.1).

assumptions.gap: The exact definition of the reported single-parameter % error for α is not given beyond the general metric sentence.
assumptions.quote: Errors are reported in percent of the actual value, as the median over the estimated parameters of a model.

assumptions.gap: The initial state x0 is estimated jointly but the paper does not state whether positivity or bounds are imposed on x0.
assumptions.chosen: Unconstrained least squares, as in the augmented linear system.
assumptions.quote: The initial state x0 is treated as n additional unknowns

assumptions.gap: The exact ODE solver tolerances for the synthetic SIDR data generation are not stated in the main text.
assumptions.quote: integrated with LSODA (Petzold, 1983) at relative and absolute tolerances of 10−10.

assumptions.gap: The printed Δt=5.05 days is rounded; the exact grid construction is not shown.
The population is printed as 59·10^6 in OCR text; the exact integer is not otherwise specified.
The paper does not say whether any smoothing is applied to noisy states before evaluating the library inside the PIWR integrals.
assumptions.chosen: No smoothing; use noisy states directly in the library and integrate by spline.
assumptions.quote: Both PIR and PIWR evaluate the library at the noisy samples.

assumptions.gap: The least-squares rank-deficiency threshold and exact SVD/LAPACK routine are not specified.

assumptions.gap: The exact joint prior box for α, β, γ in the SIDR calibration is not tabulated parameter by parameter.
assumptions.chosen: Independent uniform [0.5α*,1.5α*], [0.5β*,1.5β*], [0.5γ*,1.5γ*], with no cap binding since all values are below 1.

assumptions.gap: The random seeds for the 100 row-scaling tuning draws and 200 Rbar tuning draws are not given.
assumptions.chosen: Use separate fixed seeds for row-scaling tuning, Rbar tuning, calibration, and testing.
assumptions.quote: Every estimator is tuned on draws that are not used for calibration or testing: the row scaling on 100 draws,  ̄R on 200 draws.

assumptions.gap: The seed splitting for 999 calibration problems and 2,000 test problems is not specified.

assumptions.gap: Whether coverage is evaluated for all parameters simultaneously or marginally is not fully explicit in the table rows.

assumptions.gap: The numerical precision and implementation language for the least-squares solve are not part of the mathematical method but affect exact values.

assumptions.gap: Whether the RACC h factor is used for the point estimate or only for interval widths is not explicit in the score formula text.

assumptions.gap: The paper does not state whether the first and last samples are included in the PIWR linear system beyond saying all samples are used.

assumptions.gap: The paper does not constrain the SIDR parameter estimates to be positive or within a physical range.

assumptions.quote: PIR and PIWR search an unbounded parameter space

why: The only linked repository (Shaier/DINN) is the *baseline* the paper benchmarks against, not the paper's own method: it contains 626 files of Jupyter notebooks and CSVs for DINN training, zero Python modules, and no PIWR / PIR-FD / conformal-prediction code at all. The paper's contribution (physics-informed weak regression: integrate the linear-in-parameters SIDR equations in time with cubic-spline quadrature, solve a closed-form least-squares problem with the initial state as a free unknown) exists only as a mathematical description in the text, so it must be reimplemented. The repo is still useful in one narrow way: Diseases/COVID/generate_covid_data.ipynb and sidr.csv pin down the exact SIDR benchmark (N = 59e6, S0 = N-1, I0 = 1, alpha = 0.191, beta = 0.05, gamma = 0.0294, 100 points on [0,500], 1% multiplicative noise), which is the match target for C1, and the data can equally be regenerated from Appendix A.1 alone. The reimplementation is cheap: a 4-state linear ODE system, a cumulative-spline quadrature matrix, and one numpy.linalg.lstsq call.
est_runtime: 5-10 minutes of command time: ~1 min to install numpy/scipy/matplotlib, ~10 s to simulate the SIDR benchmark, milliseconds per PIWR fit, so a few hundred repeated fits plus a noise-level sweep finish in seconds; the remainder is development of the ~200-line weak-form estimator and the clean re-run.
blockers: The linked repository is the DINN baseline (PyTorch 1.8.1, pandas 1.1.5, numpy 1.19.2, Python 3.6) — the paper's own estimator is not in it, so nothing in the repo produces any of the claimed numbers

requirements.txt pins torch/numpy versions that will not install cleanly on this machine's Python 3.12, but that is moot since the DINN baseline is the comparison method and not needed for the match target
No scripts, only notebooks; no CLI entrypoint that emits a target number

The two runs reported for C1 are single noise realizations implicitly (no seed stated), so an exact 0.124% match requires reproducing the same random draw; honest reproduction should report median/mean over realizations and accept a small deviation

approach: Reimplement PIWR for the SIDR benchmark directly from the equations: generate the true trajectory with LSODA at 1e-10 tolerances, and for C1 use the 100-point DINN `sidr.csv` 1% benchmark when available (falling back to a fixed-seed regeneration from Appendix A.1) so the single noise realisation is not invented. For each compartment and each library column, evaluate A(x,t) on the sample grid, interpolate with a not-a-knot cubic spline, integrate the spline exactly to every sample time, and assemble the augmented linear system with x0 as four extra unknowns. Solve the column-normalised system with `numpy.linalg.lstsq` (never forming normal equations), unscale, extract theta=(alpha,beta,gamma), and compute |alpha_hat-0.191|/0.191*100. Add noiseless, stability-over-realizations, and timing checks, then write all numbers to `results/metrics.json`.
steps: Create `config.py` with the exact SIDR parameters, time grid, noise level, LSODA tolerances, spline/quadrature settings, column scaling, lstsq settings, target and tolerance; do not install DINN requirements or run DINN notebooks.
Implement `src/sidr.py`: SIDR RHS with state order [S,I,D,R], LSODA simulation at rtol=atol=1e-10, compartment-wise Gaussian noise per R7, and a flexible CSV loader for the DINN `sidr.csv` benchmark.

Load `Diseases/COVID/sidr.csv` if present; inspect header/columns and confirm there are 100 rows with time plus S,I,D,R. Compare it with a noiseless LSODA trajectory to verify it is the 1% noise file. If it is missing or not the 1% file, use `Experiments/noise/sidr_100_pts.csv`; if no candidate CSV exists, regenerate with seed 0.

Implement `src/piwr.py`: for each state c and each library column k, evaluate A_{c,k}(x_noisy(t_i),t_i) on the sample grid, build a not-a-knot CubicSpline, integrate exactly from t_0 to every t_j via the spline antiderivative, and store J[c][j,k].

Build the augmented system M and RHS y: for each state c and time j, set M[row,c]=1 for x0_c and M[row,n_states+k]=J[c][j,k] for theta_k; set y[row]=x_noisy[j,c]. Include all m samples and ensure J[:,0]=0 at j=0.

Column-scale M to unit column norms, solve with `numpy.linalg.lstsq(M_scaled,y,rcond=None)` in float64, unscale coefficients by dividing by the column norms, and extract x0_hat and theta_hat=(alpha_hat,beta_hat,gamma_hat).

Run the noiseless sanity fit on the true trajectory: verify alpha_hat is within about 1e-4% of 0.191 and x0_hat matches the true initial state; if not, debug the SIDR library, spline integration, or state/column mapping before touching the 1% data.
Run the C1 fit on the verified 1% benchmark CSV: compute alpha_hat and `100*abs(alpha_hat-0.191)/0.191`; record whether it lies in [0.1116,0.1364].
Run the stability sweep: regenerate 1000 independent 1% noise realisations with fixed seeds, fit each with PIWR, and store median, mean, IQR and 5–95% range of the alpha percent error.
Run the timing check: repeat the PIWR fit 30 times on the C1 data set and record median CPU milliseconds per fit.

Write `results/metrics.json` with the C1 headline fields (alpha_true, alpha_hat, alpha_rel_error_pct, target_pct, within_tolerance), data source, matrix shape/rank/condition number, x0_hat, beta_hat, gamma_hat, noiseless check, stability summary, timing summary, and the exact config used.

Validate the JSON by re-reading it and printing a summary; verify the headline error is compared against the relative tolerance band and that the noiseless, stability and timing diagnostics are present.
smoke_test: Implement a `--smoke` mode in `reproduce.py` that loads/simulates the SIDR benchmark once, builds M, asserts M.shape==(400,7), asserts J_0==0, checks rank(M_scaled)==7, and runs two fits: (i) noiseless true states, expected alpha error below 1e-4%, and (ii) one noisy 1% realisation, expected alpha error in the 0.05–1% range. This proves the spline quadrature, augmented least squares, scaling, and alpha extraction without the 1000-realisation sweep.
intermediate_checks: Dataset size: t has shape (100,), X_noisy has shape (100,4), all finite; time runs from 0 to 500 inclusive with `np.linspace(0,500,100)`.
True trajectory sanity: S decreases from N-1, I starts at 1 and peaks, D and R are nonnegative and nondecreasing; max absolute value per compartment is nonzero so the R7 noise scale is well defined.

Noise sanity on the benchmark CSV: if using `sidr.csv`, compare it with the noiseless trajectory and verify residuals are approximately N(0, (0.01*max|x_c|)^2); if not, select the correct 100-point 1% noise CSV before fitting.
Matrix sanity: M has shape (4*100,4+3)=(400,7); J at t_0 is exactly zero for every column; after unit-column scaling no column has zero norm; rank is 7 and the scaled condition number is reported.

Noiseless baseline: a PIWR fit to the true states recovers alpha to near machine/quadrature accuracy (target <1e-4% relative error) and gives x0 close to [N-1,1,0,0]; failure here means an equation/library/quadrature bug, not a noise issue.
Single noisy fit sanity: alpha_hat is positive and within a few percent of 0.191; the reported C1 error should be near the paper's 0.124%, not orders of magnitude larger.
Timing sanity: 30 repeated fits on the 100-point SIDR problem should be milliseconds or less on CPU; if a fit takes seconds, the implementation is rebuilding splines or solving the wrong problem.
budget_plan: About 10 minutes of command time: 2 min creating `config.py`, `src/sidr.py`, `src/piwr.py`, `src/evaluate.py`, and `reproduce.py`; 2 min on smoke/noiseless validation and fixing any shape or quadrature bug; 3 min on the C1 fit plus the 1000-realisation stability sweep (each fit is sub-millisecond to millisecond, so the sweep is dominated by data generation and Python overhead); 1 min for the 30-repeat timing check; 2 min for writing, re-reading, and validating `results/metrics.json`.

A preprint - October 15, 2026
A physics-based model can generate its own calibration population, which makes split conformal prediction
applicable to model parameters. The resulting simultaneous intervals keep their 90 % coverage in all 88 tested
settings of the DINN benchmarks, and in the S3I3R and real-data cases, are narrow where the estimate is
accurate, and widen where the data do not support the estimate, without access to the true parameters. The
residual-adaptive factor (PIWR-RACC) adapts the width to the difficulty of the individual data set at no
cost in coverage (in the time-varying Case 3 it narrows the bands by a factor of nine). Prior knowledge enters
the same way, where a parameter known only approximately must be drawn from its uncertainty range in
the calibration population, otherwise the intervals lose their coverage, and fixing a parameter narrows the
intervals only of the parameters it decouples.

"""COVID-19 SIDR benchmark: model RHS, LSODA simulation, noise, CSV loading.

Model (paper Appendix A.1, eq. 28), state x = (S, I, D, R), population N:
    dS/dt = -alpha*S*I/N
    dI/dt =  alpha*S*I/N - (beta + gamma)*I
    dD/dt =  gamma*I
    dR/dt =  beta*I
The library A(x, t) of eq. (5) (used by PIWR) lives in src/piwr.py.
"""
import numpy as np
from scipy.integrate import odeint


def rhs(x, t, alpha, beta, gamma, N):
    """SIDR right-hand side, state order (S, I, D, R)."""
    S, I, D, R = x
    si = S * I / N
    return [
        -alpha * si,
        alpha * si - (beta + gamma) * I,
        gamma * I,
        beta * I,
    ]


def simulate(t, params, x0, N, rtol=1e-10, atol=1e-10):
    """Integrate the SIDR model with LSODA (scipy.integrate.odeint) at the
    paper's tolerances (R15). Returns X with shape (len(t), 4)."""
    alpha, beta, gamma = params
    X = odeint(rhs, x0, t, args=(alpha, beta, gamma, N), rtol=rtol, atol=atol)
    return np.asarray(X, dtype=np.float64)


def add_noise(X, eps, rng):
    """Compartment-wise measurement noise (Section 5.1, R7):
        x_tilde_c(t_i) = x_c(t_i) + eps * max_t |x_c(t)| * xi_i,
    xi_i i.i.d. N(0, 1), independent per compartment and time.  The scale uses
    the maximum of the *true* trajectory (A18)."""
    scale = eps * np.max(np.abs(X), axis=0)          # one scale per compartment
    return X + scale * rng.standard_normal(X.shape)


def load_dinn_csv(path):
    """Load a DINN SIDR csv (rows: t, S, I, D, R, each of length m).

    Returns (t, X) with X shape (m, 4).  The DINN files store the noise-free
    trajectory generated with scipy.integrate.odeint at default tolerances;
    they are used here only as an independent cross-check of the simulation.
    """
    arr = np.loadtxt(path, delimiter=",")
    if arr.shape[0] == 5:          # rows are (t, S, I, D, R)
        t, S, I, D, R = arr
    elif arr.shape[1] == 5:        # columns are (t, S, I, D, R)
        t, S, I, D, R = arr.T
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"unexpected SIDR csv shape {arr.shape} in {path}")
    X = np.column_stack([S, I, D, R])
    return t, X

args.content:
"""Physics-informed weak regression (PIWR), paper Section 3.2.

The SIDR model is linear in the coefficient vector theta = (alpha, beta, gamma):

    d/dt [S, I, D, R]^T = A(x, t) theta,

with the library (eq. 5)

    A(x, t) = [[-S*I/N,   0,   0],
               [ S*I/N,  -I,  -I],
               [     0,   0,   I],
               [     0,   I,   0]]

so that dS = -alpha SI/N, dI = alpha SI/N - beta I - gamma I, dD = gamma I,
dR = beta I.  The library contains no unknown parameters (R1).

PIWR integrates the model in time instead of differentiating the data (R2):

    x(t_j) = x0 + J_j theta,   J_j = int_{t_0}^{t_j} A(x(s), s) ds.

Each library entry is interpolated over the sample grid by a cubic spline
(not-a-knot end conditions) and the spline is integrated exactly (R3).  The
initial state x0 is estimated jointly with theta through the augmented system
(R4), which is solved by an SVD-based least squares after scaling the columns
to unit norm (R5, R6); the normal equations are never formed.
"""
import numpy as np
from scipy.interpolate import CubicSpline

N_DEFAULT = 59e6


def library_sidr(X, N=N_DEFAULT):
    """Evaluate the SIDR library A(x, t) on the sample grid.

    X : (m, 4) array with columns S, I, D, R (possibly noisy samples).
    Returns A of shape (m, 4, 3) with A[i, c, k] = (A)_{c,k} at sample i.
    """
    S, I, D, R = X.T
    si_over_n = S * I / N
    m = X.shape[0]
    A = np.zeros((m, 4, 3), dtype=np.float64)
    A[:, 0, 0] = -si_over_n          # dS/dt row: -SI/N * alpha
    A[:, 1, 0] = si_over_n           # dI/dt row:  SI/N * alpha
    A[:, 1, 1] = -I                  # dI/dt row: -I * beta
    A[:, 1, 2] = -I                  # dI/dt row: -I * gamma
    A[:, 2, 2] = I                   # dD/dt row:  I * gamma
    A[:, 3, 1] = I                   # dR/dt row:  I * beta
    return A


def quadrature_weights(t, bc_type="not-a-knot"):
    """Quadrature-weight matrix W of eq. (13) (paper Section 3.2, R3).

    W[j, i] are weights such that, for samples f_i = f(t_i),
        sum_i W[j, i] f_i  ~=  int_{t_0}^{t_j} f(s) ds,
    obtained by interpolating f with a cubic spline (not-a-knot end
    conditions) and integrating the spline exactly.  Because the spline is
    linear in its data, the weights depend only on the time grid and are
    computed once per grid.

    Implementation: interpolate the m cardinal (identity) data vectors with
    one vector-valued CubicSpline and take its exact antiderivative.
    """
    t = np.asarray(t, dtype=np.float64)
    m = t.shape[0]
    cardinal = CubicSpline(t, np.eye(m), bc_type=bc_type)   # basis i is column i
    anti = cardinal.antiderivative()                        # exact antiderivative
    vals = np.asarray(anti(t), dtype=np.float64)            # vals[i, j] = F_i(t_j)
    W = (vals - vals[:, [0]]).T                             # W[j, i] = F_i(t_j)-F_i(t_0)
    W[0, :] = 0.0                                           # J_0 = 0 exactly (eq. 13)
    return W


def _assemble(t, X_noisy, library, W):
    """Stack the integrated relations x(t_j) = x0 + J_j theta into M, y (eq. 14).

    Unknown vector z = (x0, theta) in R^{n+p}; each time j contributes the
    block row [I_n | J_j] and right-hand side x_tilde_j.
    """
    m = t.shape[0]
    n = X_noisy.shape[1]
    A_vals = library(X_noisy)                                # (m, n, p)
    p = A_vals.shape[2]
    J = np.einsum("ji,ick->jck", W, A_vals, optimize=True)   # J[j, c, k] = (J_j)_{c,k}
    M = np.zeros((n * m, n + p), dtype=np.float64)
    y = np.zeros(n * m, dtype=np.float64)
    eye = np.eye(n)
    for j in range(m):
        r = slice(j * n, (j + 1) * n)
        M[r, :n] = eye
        M[r, n:] = J[j]
        y[r] = X_noisy[j]
    return M, y, J


def piwr_fit(t, X_noisy, library=library_sidr, W=None, row_scaling=None):
    """One PIWR fit.  Returns (theta_hat, x0_hat, diagnostics).

    t          : (m,) sample times (equally spaced grid, endpoints included)
    X_noisy    : (m, n) measured states
    library    : callable X -> (m, n, p) library A evaluated at the samples
    W          : precomputed quadrature weights for the grid (computed if None)
    row_scaling: None -> D_n = I_n;  "compartment_max" -> D_n = diag(1/s_c)
                 with s_c = max_i |x_tilde_{i,c}| (eq. 10, chosen per model
                 on tuning draws, Section 5.1)
    """
    t = np.asarray(t, dtype=np.float64)
    X_noisy = np.asarray(X_noisy, dtype=np.float64)
    m, n = X_noisy.shape
    if W is None:
        W = quadrature_weights(t)
    M, y, J = _assemble(t, X_noisy, library, W)
    p = M.shape[1] - n

    # Optional row scaling D = I_m (x) D_n (turns the problem into a weighted
    # least squares; decided per model on tuning draws, Section 3.2/5.1).
    if row_scaling == "compartment_max":
        s = np.max(np.abs(X_noisy), axis=0)
        row_mult = np.tile(1.0 / s, m)
        M = M * row_mult[:, None]
        y = y * row_mult
    elif row_scaling is not None:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown row_scaling {row_scaling!r}")

    # Column scaling to unit norm before the solve (R6); a diagonal change of
    # variables that leaves the minimizer unchanged.
    col_norms = np.linalg.norm(M, axis=0)
    col_norms[col_norms == 0.0] = 1.0
    Ms = M / col_norms

    # SVD-based least squares (numpy.linalg.lstsq); the normal equations are
    # never formed (R5).
    u_hat, _, rank, sv = np.linalg.lstsq(Ms, y, rcond=None)
    z_hat = u_hat / col_norms
    x0_hat = z_hat[:n]
    theta_hat = z_hat[n:]

    resid = M @ z_hat - y
    diagnostics = {
        "M_shape": list(M.shape),
        "rank": int(rank),
        "cond_scaled": float(sv[0] / sv[-1]) if sv.size and sv[-1] > 0 else np.inf,
        "residual_norm": float(np.linalg.norm(resid)),
        "rel_residual": float(np.linalg.norm(resid) / np.linalg.norm(y)),
        "row_scaling": row_scaling,
    }
    return theta_hat, x0_hat, diagnostics

import numpy as np

from src.piwr import piwr_fit
from src.sidr import add_noise


def pct_error(estimate, actual):
    """Percent of the actual value (paper Section 5.1, R14)."""
    return 100.0 * abs(estimate - actual) / abs(actual)

"""Reproduce claim C1: PIWR estimates the COVID-19 SIDR transmission rate
alpha with 0.124 % relative error at 1 % measurement noise
(arXiv:2610.19058, Table 2, row alpha, eps = 0.01).

Protocol (paper Sections 2, 3, 5.1 and Appendix A.1):
  1. Simulate the SIDR benchmark with LSODA at rtol=atol=1e-10 (R13, R15).
  2. Add 1 % compartment-wise noise (R7) with a fixed seed (point estimate).
  3. Fit PIWR: cubic-spline quadrature (R3), joint initial state (R4),
     unit-column scaling (R6), SVD least squares (R5).
  4. Check stability over 1,000 noise realizations and time 30 repeated fits.

Usage:
    python reproduce.py           full run, writes results/metrics.json
    python reproduce.py --smoke   fast self-check of the estimator only
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import sys

import numpy as np

import config
from src.evaluate import (
    alpha_error_sweep,
    median_param_error,
    pct_error,
    summarize,
    time_fits,
    tune_row_scaling,
)
from src.piwr import library_sidr, piwr_fit, quadrature_weights, _assemble
from src.sidr import add_noise, load_dinn_csv, simulate

N = config.POPULATION_N
X0_TRUE = config.X0_TRUE
PARAMS_TRUE = config.TRUE_PARAMS
ALPHA_TRUE = PARAMS_TRUE[0]
T_GRID = config.TIME_GRID
EPS = config.NOISE_EPS
SEEDS_STABILITY = [config.STABILITY_SEED + k for k in range(config.STABILITY_REALIZATIONS)]


def check_true_trajectory(X_true):
    """Intermediate checks: shapes, finiteness, and qualitative SIDR behaviour."""
    assert X_true.shape == (100, 4), f"shape {X_true.shape}"
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(X_true))
    S, I, D, R = X_true.T
    assert np.all(np.diff(S) < 1e-6), "S must be nonincreasing"
    assert np.all(np.diff(D) > -1e-6), "D must be nondecreasing"
    assert np.all(np.diff(R) > -1e-6), "R must be nondecreasing"
    assert np.all(I >= 0) and np.all(D >= 0) and np.all(R >= 0)
    assert S[0] == X0_TRUE[0] and I[0] == 1.0 and D[0] == 0.0 and R[0] == 0.0
    scale = EPS * np.max(np.abs(X_true), axis=0)
    assert np.all(scale > 0.0), "noise scale must be nonzero for all compartments"


def check_csv_agreement(csv_path):
    """Cross-check the simulation against the DINN generator file (repo)."""
    t_csv, X_csv = load_dinn_csv(csv_path)
    X_true = simulate(T_GRID, PARAMS_TRUE, X0_TRUE, N,
                      config.SOLVER_RTOL, config.SOLVER_ATOL)
    # compare on the common grid (both use np.linspace(0,500,100))
    denom = np.maximum(np.abs(X_csv), 1.0)
    rel = np.max(np.abs(X_csv - X_true) / denom)
    return {"csv": csv_path, "max_rel_diff_vs_LSODA_1e-10": float(rel)}


def smoke_checks():
    """Fast end-to-end check of spline quadrature + augmented least squares."""
    t = T_GRID
    X_true = simulate(t, PARAMS_TRUE, X0_TRUE, N, config.SOLVER_RTOL, config.SOLVER_ATOL)
    check_true_trajectory(X_true)

    # quadrature weights: exact for cubics, O(dt^4) in general (eq. 13)
    W = quadrature_weights(t, config.SPLINE_BC)
    assert W.shape == (100, 100)
    assert np.allclose(W[0, :], 0.0, atol=1e-12), "J_0 must vanish (eq. 13)"
    f = np.cos(t / 100.0)                       # smooth test integrand
    exact = 100.0 * np.sin(t / 100.0) - 100.0 * np.sin(t[0] / 100.0)
    quad_err = np.max(np.abs(W @ f - exact))
    assert quad_err < 1e-2, f"spline quadrature inaccurate: {quad_err}"

    # matrix sanity (eq. 14): (400, 7), full rank, finite conditioning
    X_noisy = add_noise(X_true, EPS, np.random.default_rng(123))
    M, y, J = _assemble(t, X_noisy, library_sidr, W)
    assert M.shape == (400, 7), f"M shape {M.shape}"
    assert np.allclose(J[0], 0.0, atol=1e-12), "J_0 must vanish"
    col_norms = np.linalg.norm(M, axis=0)
    assert np.all(col_norms > 0.0)
    Ms = M / col_norms
    rank = np.linalg.matrix_rank(Ms)
    assert rank == 7, f"rank {rank}"
    cond = np.linalg.cond(Ms)
    assert np.isfinite(cond)

    # (i) noiseless fit must recover alpha to quadrature accuracy (~1e-4 %)
    theta_nl, x0_nl, diag = piwr_fit(t, X_true, library=library_sidr, W=W, row_scaling=None)
    alpha_err_nl = pct_error(theta_nl[0], ALPHA_TRUE)
    assert alpha_err_nl < 1e-2, f"noiseless alpha err {alpha_err_nl} %"

    # (ii) one 1 % noise realization: plausible error range (0.05-1 %)
    theta_n, x0_n, diag_n = piwr_fit(t, X_noisy, library=library_sidr, W=W, row_scaling=None)
    alpha_err_n = pct_error(theta_n[0], ALPHA_TRUE)
    assert 0.05 < alpha_err_n < 1.0, f"noisy alpha err {alpha_err_n} %"

    print("[smoke] all checks passed")
    print(f"[smoke] quadrature max err on cos(t/100): {quad_err:.2e}")
    print(f"[smoke] rank(M)={rank}, cond(Ms)={cond:.2f}")
    print(f"[smoke] noiseless alpha_hat={theta_nl[0]:.10f} "
          f"({alpha_err_nl:.3e} %), x0_hat={np.round(x0_nl, 3)}")
    print(f"[smoke] noisy    alpha_hat={theta_n[0]:.6f} ({alpha_err_n:.3f} %)")
    return True


def full_run():
    t = T_GRID
    print("[1/6] simulating SIDR benchmark (LSODA, rtol=atol=1e-10) ...")
    X_true = simulate(t, PARAMS_TRUE, X0_TRUE, N, config.SOLVER_RTOL, config.SOLVER_ATOL)
    check_true_trajectory(X_true)
    compartment_max = np.max(np.abs(X_true), axis=0)

    csv_report = None
    for path in ("repo/Diseases/COVID/sidr.csv", "repo/Experiments/noise/sidr_100_pts.csv"):
        if os.path.exists(path):
            csv_report = check_csv_agreement(path)
            break

    W = quadrature_weights(t, config.SPLINE_BC)
    assert W.shape == (100, 100) and np.allclose(W[0, :], 0.0, atol=1e-12)

    print("[3/6] tuning row scaling on 100 draws (paper Section 5.1) ...")
    tuning_seeds = [config.TUNING_SEED + k for k in range(config.TUNING_DRAWS)]
    row_scaling, tuning_report = tune_row_scaling(
        t, X_true, EPS, tuning_seeds, PARAMS_TRUE, library_sidr, W,
        config.ROW_SCALING_CANDIDATES,
    )

    print("[4/6] C1 fit: 1 % noise, single fixed-seed realization ...")
    rng = np.random.default_rng(config.POINT_SEED)
    X_c1 = add_noise(X_true, EPS, rng)

def tune_row_scaling(t, X_true, eps, seeds, params_true, library, W, candidates):
    """Pick the row-scaling setting on tuning draws (paper Section 5.1).

    For each candidate setting we draw noisy data sets at the literature values
    (on seeds distinct from the point estimate / stability seeds), fit PIWR,
    and average the per-draw median parameter error; the setting with the
    smaller value is selected.  Returns (chosen_setting, tuning_report)."""
    report = {}
    best, best_score = None, np.inf
    for cand in candidates:
        med_errs = np.empty(len(seeds))
        alpha_errs = np.empty(len(seeds))
        for k, s in enumerate(seeds):
            theta_hat, _, _ = fit_noisy(t, X_true, eps, s, library, W, cand)
            med_errs[k] = median_param_error(theta_hat, params_true)
            alpha_errs[k] = pct_error(theta_hat[0], params_true[0])
        score = float(np.mean(med_errs))
        report[str(cand)] = {
            "mean_of_median_param_error_pct": score,
            "median_alpha_error_pct": float(np.median(alpha_errs)),
            "mean_alpha_error_pct": float(np.mean(alpha_errs)),
        }
        if score < best_score:
            best, best_score = cand, score
    report["chosen"] = str(best)
    return best, report

"""Reproduce claim C1: PIWR estimates the COVID-19 SIDR transmission rate
alpha with 0.124 % relative error at 1 % measurement noise
(arXiv:2610.19058, Table 2, row alpha, eps = 0.01).

Protocol (paper Sections 2, 3, 5.1 and Appendix A.1):
  1. SIDR benchmark data. If a DINN 1 % noise CSV exists it is consumed
     directly; otherwise the trajectory is simulated with LSODA at
     rtol=atol=1e-10 (R13, R15) and 1 % compartment-wise noise is added (R7)
     with fixed seeds.  The noiseless DINN `sidr.csv`, when present, is used
     as a cross-check of the simulation.
  2. PIWR fit: cubic-spline quadrature (R3), joint initial state (R4),
     unit-column scaling (R6), SVD least squares (R5); D_n = I (A2).
  3. Primary diagnostic: median alpha % error over 1,000 noise realizations.
     Single fixed-seed realization (seed 0) and a compartment-max row-scaling
     variant are reported side by side; a DINN-style multiplicative-noise
     sweep diagnoses the noise/data source.

Usage:
    python reproduce.py           full run, writes results/metrics.json
    python reproduce.py --smoke   fast self-check of the estimator only
"""
import argparse
import json
import os

import numpy as np

import config
from src.evaluate import (
    alpha_error_sweep,
    median_param_error,
    pct_error,
    summarize,
    time_fits,
)
from src.piwr import _assemble, library_sidr, piwr_fit, quadrature_weights
from src.sidr import (
    add_noise,
    add_noise_multiplicative,
    load_dinn_csv,
    simulate,
)

N = config.POPULATION_N
X0_TRUE = config.X0_TRUE
PARAMS_TRUE = config.TRUE_PARAMS
ALPHA_TRUE = PARAMS_TRUE[0]
T_GRID = config.TIME_GRID
EPS = config.NOISE_EPS
ROW_SCALING = config.ROW_SCALING            # D_n = I for SIDR (A2)
SEEDS_STABILITY = [config.STABILITY_SEED + k for k in range(config.STABILITY_REALIZATIONS)]
CANDIDATE_CSVS = (
    "repo/Diseases/COVID/sidr.csv",
    "repo/Experiments/noise/sidr_100_pts.csv",
)
STATE_NAMES = config.STATE_ORDER


def check_true_trajectory(X_true):
    """Intermediate checks: shapes, finiteness, qualitative SIDR behaviour."""
    assert X_true.shape == (100, 4), f"shape {X_true.shape}"
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(X_true))
    S, I, D, R = X_true.T
    assert np.all(np.diff(S) < 1e-6), "S must be nonincreasing"
    assert np.all(np.diff(D) > -1e-6), "D must be nondecreasing"
    assert np.all(np.diff(R) > -1e-6), "R must be nondecreasing"
    assert np.all(I >= 0) and np.all(D >= 0) and np.all(R >= 0)
    assert S[0] == X0_TRUE[0] and I[0] == 1.0 and D[0] == 0.0 and R[0] == 0.0
    scale = EPS * np.max(np.abs(X_true), axis=0)
    assert np.all(scale > 0.0), "noise scale must be nonzero for all compartments"


def resolve_data_source():
    """Locate the C1 data set.

    A DINN 1 % noise file, if present, is consumed directly.  Candidate CSVs
    are tested against the R7 noise model (residual std vs simulation should
    be ~ eps*max|x_c| for a noise file).  Otherwise the benchmark is
    regenerated (LSODA, 1e-10) and noised with fixed seeds, and a noiseless
    DINN CSV (if present) is used only as a simulation cross-check.
    """
    t = T_GRID
    X_true = simulate(t, PARAMS_TRUE, X0_TRUE, N, config.SOLVER_RTOL, config.SOLVER_ATOL)
    check_true_trajectory(X_true)
    scale = EPS * np.max(np.abs(X_true), axis=0)

    csv_checks = []
    consumed = None
    for path in CANDIDATE_CSVS:
        if not os.path.exists(path):
            csv_checks.append({"path": path, "exists": False})
            continue
        t_csv, X_csv = load_dinn_csv(path)
        resid_std = (X_csv - X_true).std(axis=0)
        ratio = resid_std / scale
        is_r7_noise_file = bool(np.all(ratio > 0.5))   # ~1.0 for a 1% file
        max_rel = float(np.max(np.abs(X_csv - X_true) / np.maximum(np.abs(X_csv), 1.0)))
        csv_checks.append({
            "path": path,
            "exists": True,
            "is_r7_1pct_noise_file": is_r7_noise_file,
            "residual_std_over_r7_noise_scale": [float(v) for v in ratio],
            "max_rel_diff_vs_simulation": max_rel,
        })
        if is_r7_noise_file and consumed is None:
            consumed = (path, t_csv, X_csv)

    if consumed is not None:
        path, t_csv, X_csv = consumed
        source = {
            "origin": "DINN noise CSV consumed directly",
            "csv": path,
            "base": "CSV data (already carries the 1 % noise)",
        }
        return t_csv, X_csv, X_true, source, csv_checks

    noiseless_csv = next((c["path"] for c in csv_checks
                          if c.get("exists") and not c.get("is_r7_1pct_noise_file")), None)
    source = {
        "origin": "regenerated benchmark + fixed-seed R7 noise",
        "csv": noiseless_csv,
        "base": "LSODA rtol=atol=1e-10 simulation; 1 % noise per R7 added with "
                "fixed seeds (POINT_SEED for the single realization, "
                "STABILITY_SEED+k for the sweep)",
        "reason": "no DINN 1 % SIDR CSV present (repo CSVs are noiseless "
                  "generator outputs; DINN adds unseeded noise at train time)",
    }
    return t, X_true, X_true, source, csv_checks

    """Fast end-to-end check of spline quadrature + augmented least squares."""

    W = quadrature_weights(t, config.SPLINE_BC)

target.statement: PIWR estimates the COVID-19 SIDR transmission rate α with 0.124 % relative error at 1 % measurement noise.
target.table_ref: Table 2, row α, column PIWR / PIWR-RACC under noise level ε = 0.01

tolerance.why: Rule 4: the target is a relative % error with no reported std for this row and is an unbounded error metric, so use a 10 % relative band around 0.124 %, i.e. about 0.1116–0.1364 % error.

audit_summary: PIWR is implemented faithfully for the SIDR benchmark: parameter-linear library, integrated weak relation with not-a-knot cubic-spline quadrature, joint initial state, SVD least squares with unit-column scaling, and the paper's additive eps*max|x_c| noise; the noiseless alpha error (3.8e-5%) matches the magnitude of C2. The C1 headline is 1.078% alpha error at eps=0.01, about 8.7x the paper's 0.124% and far outside the 10% tolerance band; the 1000-realization distribution has median 0.717% (p05 0.0635%, p95 2.11%), so the claim lies in the lower tail of the additive-noise distribution rather than at its centre. The likely dominant cause is a paper/claim inconsistency in the noise model: the claim contract and DINN notebooks use multiplicative per-point noise, whose diagnostic median (0.28%) falls inside the paper's quoted 0.12-0.49% range, whereas the implementer ran the additive R7 formula (median 0.717%). The estimator itself is not buggy (noiseless recovery is exact), so the remaining causes are the unstated seed (A1), row-scaling (A2) and smoothing (A8) ambiguities, and randomness. No hard-coded result or echo of the paper number was found (0.124 appears only in config's CLAIM_CHECK for the band test), the run is not scaled down, and the conformal/RACC/delta-method components (R8-R12) are absent because the target is a single point fit.

requirement_check.evidence: src/piwr.py library_sidr builds the parameter-linear library A=[[-SI/N,0,0],[SI/N,-I,-I],[0,0,I],[0,I,0]] with theta=(alpha,beta,gamma); A contains no unknowns and the map h is the identity on these coefficients.
src/piwr.py _assemble builds the integrated relation x_j = x0 + J_j theta with J[j,c,k]=sum_i W[j,i] A[i,c,k]; data themselves enter, no finite-difference derivative is formed.

quadrature_weights uses scipy.interpolate.CubicSpline(t, eye(m), bc_type='not-a-knot').antiderivative(); W[0,:]=0. The command ledger shows the earlier column/row indexing bug was found and fixed, and the smoke test confirms cos(t/100) integration accuracy.
_assemble sets M[r,:n]=eye(n), y[r]=X_noisy[j], so x0 is estimated jointly as n free unknowns alongside theta.
piwr_fit solves with np.linalg.lstsq(Ms, y, rcond=None) (SVD/LAPACK); normal equations are never formed.
col_norms=np.linalg.norm(M,axis=0); Ms=M/col_norms; z_hat=u_hat/col_norms — unit-column scaling before the solve and un-scaling after.

src/sidr.py add_noise returns X + (eps*np.max(np.abs(X),axis=0))*rng.standard_normal(X.shape), i.e. x + eps*max_t|x_c|*xi per compartment, exactly Section 5.1/R7; noise std is verified against the trajectory before fitting.
No conformal calibration prior box (+/-50% around literature values, capped) is implemented; the reproduction targets only the point-estimate claim C1, so the calibration population is out of scope.
No maximum-normalized-error split-conformal nonconformity score or simultaneous quantile is implemented.
No PIWR-RACC residual-adaptive factor h=1+R/Rbar (200 tuning draws) is implemented.
No 999-calibration / alpha=0.1 conformal procedure is present; only the point-estimate fit is run.
No delta-method propagation of coefficient covariance to physical parameters is implemented; only the point estimate is reported.
src/evaluate.py pct_error=100*|estimate-actual|/|actual| and median_param_error takes the median over parameters.
src/sidr.py simulate calls scipy.integrate.odeint(rhs, x0, t, ..., rtol=1e-10, atol=1e-10).

divergence_causes: paper_underspecified (A1, A2, A8, A19): the exact single-realization seed is unstated; row scaling and smoothing choices are ambiguous; and the paper's Section 5.1 additive eps*max|x_c| formula conflicts with the claim contract/DINN multiplicative per-point noise. The code ran additive R7, whose 1000-realization median (0.717%) is well above the claim, while the labelled multiplicative diagnostic median (0.28%) falls inside the paper's quoted 0.12-0.49% range

randomness: the seed-0 realization is a high-percentile draw (1.078%); the claim 0.124% sits near the 8th percentile of the additive-noise realization distribution (p05 0.0635%, median 0.717%, p95 2.11%)
